web_evidence.title: Verbal and Visual Representation of Women: Como agua para chocolate/Like Water for Chocolate
web_evidence.note: María Elena de Valdés’s World Literature Today study states that each chapter combines recipe discourse with Tita’s story and that the narrator repeatedly moves from a first-person culinary-instructor voice to third-person omniscient storytelling.

person_note: The novel recurrently combines a participating first-person recipe/frame narrator—Esperanza’s daughter and Tita’s great-niece—with extended third-person narration of Tita’s historical story. Quote q03309 directly exposes the closing first-person frame despite its apparent upstream misclassification as dialogue, while q03294, q03303, q03310, and q03311 expose sustained third-person story passages. Generic “you” in recipes or speech is instructional or interpersonal address, not second-person narration of a protagonist. The Tier B whole-book analysis independently confirms that the first-to-third shift recurs across the chapter structure, so the two constitutive persons support ALTERNATING. The main residual limitation is that the supplied quotes directly sample only the closing first-person frame, but the structural web evidence resolves its recurrence and role.
